title: Jahanabad Buddha
subtitle: Manglawar rock relief up the Malam Jabba road, Lower Swat

landmark.name: Jahanabad Buddha
edits: The rock face is the Atlas's procedural model: a block about 9 m wide and 10 m high at the front, its back cut into the slope; its shape and cracks are illustrative (no survey).

The Buddha in relief is drawn to the published size: the carved figure is 7 m high and 5 m wide (700 x 500 cm), its throne 1.2 m high and 3.9 m wide (120 x 390 cm) and the relief stands 0.11 m proud of the face. Its folds, hands, head and the halo are estimated from the published description and the photos; the halo is estimated.
The figure's foot is set 1 m above the ground at the face (estimated: the photos show the relief above the slope, not at the ground).
A timber viewing deck in front (about 3.6 x 1.5 m, estimated from the photos) and the boulders around it are illustrative.
No steps are mapped in OSM and none show in the photos, so no steps are drawn; the walk up from the road is traced over the ground (easiest slope on the DEM).
The Buddha's face is shown restored (the 2007 damage to the head is not drawn) and the carving's colour is painted from the photos.
The arrival height in the DEM (about 1119 m) is lower than the 1133 m in the Atlas pack; the model uses the DEM.

sources.name: Buddhist rock carving in Manglawar (Wikipedia)
sources.use: size of the Jahan-Abad-i relief (700 x 500 cm, asana 120 x 390 cm), its orientation (facing north west), its 2007 damage and restoration

osm_use: the Malam Jabba Road (S-15) to the point where the mapped departure to the Buddha begins, and the Buddha node
